source_name: NBU — Payments and Settlements portal (Платежі та розрахунки / EN mirror)
why_relevant: Top-level payments portal covering SEP, instant payments, payment infrastructure, statistics and rulebooks; the EN mirror (bank.gov.ua/en/payments) gives translated framing useful for cross-checking terminology.

source_name: NBU Board Resolution No. 80 of 25.07.2025 — Regulation on Open Banking in Ukraine (official PDF)
why_relevant: The foundational open banking secondary act: defines ASPSP/TPP duties, consent, data-exchange requirements and the compliance clock (ASPSPs given five months; API technical specification to be approved within 18 months). Core deadline-bearing document for the cell.

source_name: zakon.rada.gov.ua — official legal act database (NBU acts, Law on Payment Services)
why_relevant: Authoritative consolidated text and amendment history of the Law on Payment Services (No. 1591-IX) and all NBU resolutions implementing it; better structured for machine collection than the NBU's own PDFs and shows in-force/expiry dates.

source_name: NBU Open Banking Concept 2023 (КОНЦЕПЦІЯ відкритого банкінгу)
why_relevant: Explicitly not a normative act, but sets out the NBU's design intent, roadmap phases and Berlin Group alignment that the 2025 resolutions operationalise — indispensable for interpreting later acts and anticipating the API specification.

source_name: NBU SEP-4 / SEP-4.1 ISO 20022 rulebook document library
why_relevant: The operational rulebooks for Ukraine's electronic payment system (СЕП-4.1, live with instant credit transfers since 01.12.2024): general rules, ASPSP servicing parts, SEP-3 vs SEP-4 comparison. These documents carry the technical/go-live obligations that bind banks and their vendors.

source_name: NBU draft regulations open for public consultation (проєкти НПА / громадське обговорення)
why_relevant: Where forthcoming payment secondary acts appear before adoption, with a stated comment deadline — the earliest possible warning of new obligations (e.g. the 2026 draft on account opening/closing by payment service providers, comments to 10.08.2026; draft on PSP control over payment operations).

source_name: NBU Board Resolution No. 81 of 25.07.2025 — authorisation of non-financial payment service providers (TPPs)
why_relevant: Sets the three authorisation routes for AIS/PIS providers (non-PSP legal entities, payment institutions, e-money institutions, foreign PI branches, banks) — the gate every fintech TPP must pass, with a 31.12.2025 registration deadline and a 01.01.2027 professional-indemnity-insurance step-up.

source_name: EMA Association — Open API Group (Асоціація ЄМА)
why_relevant: The industry body that actually drafted Ukraine's open API technical specifications (Berlin Group-based) under NBU endorsement; publishes working-group membership, spec versions and status for individual/FOP vs legal-entity accounts. Closest thing to the de facto standards body.

source_name: Дебет-Кредит normative documents mirror (docs.dtkt.ua)
why_relevant: Free, fetch-friendly mirror of NBU resolutions keyed by the same official document IDs as zakon.rada — a practical fallback when the regulator's own site is bot-defended.

source_name: PSM7 — payment market trade press (psm7.com)
why_relevant: Specialised Ukrainian payments/fintech outlet that reports NBU draft acts and consultation deadlines quickly and in payments-specific framing; good early-warning tripwire and a source of vendor/acquirer reaction.

source_name: Wolf Theiss / Kinstellar / Ilyashev law-firm payments briefings (Ukraine)
why_relevant: Law firms are the fastest reliable English-language interpreters of NBU resolution numbers, authorisation routes and compliance dates; they name the exact resolutions (No. 80, No. 81 of 25.07.2025) that are hard to pin down from the regulator's site alone.

source_name: NBU English newsroom and payments section (bank.gov.ua/en)
why_relevant: Official English framing of the same acts and milestones; slower and less complete than the Ukrainian side but authoritative for terminology mapping (надавач платіжних послуг = payment service provider; НПНПП = non-financial PSP).

source_name: Berlin Group openFinance / NextGenPSD2 standards (upstream of the Ukrainian API spec)
why_relevant: Ukraine's open API specification is explicitly built on Berlin Group documentation, so upstream Berlin Group releases foreshadow what the NBU-approved Ukrainian technical specification will require of ASPSPs and vendors.

source_name: Ukrainian general business/finance press covering open banking go-live (RBC-Ukraine, Censor.net BIZ, Mind.ua, dev.ua, Minfin)
why_relevant: Carries dated statements of go-live expectations (API opening from 01.08.2025; full technical readiness no later than 01.08.2026; system-wide readiness expected Aug-Sep 2026) and NBU officials' remarks that do not always appear in formal acts.

source_name: Законотворчість — Пошук за реквізитами (Verkhovna Rada bill register search)
why_relevant: The authoritative search surface over the Verkhovna Rada bill register: every registered draft law on banking/payments, its number, initiators, lead committee and procedural stage. This is the entry point for A3 pipeline monitoring and no NBU/regulator site mirrors it.

source_name: Картка законопроєкту (individual bill card, itd.rada.gov.ua/billinfo/Bills/Card/{id})
source_subtype: bill dossier page (structured, with document attachments)
why_relevant: The per-bill dossier: registration date, subject of legislative initiative, lead and co-executing committees, attached texts (проєкт закону, пояснювальна записка, порівняльна таблиця), committee conclusions, reading dates, vote outcomes and signature/publication events. This is where entry-into-force clauses and the transition-period deadlines that NBU later implements first become visible.

source_name: Законопроєкти, що перебувають на опрацюванні в комітетах (CommBillProc)
why_relevant: Stage-specific view of which bills are currently sitting with which committee — exactly the committee-stage dimension of this cell. Lets the pipeline be sliced by lead committee (finance/tax/customs) rather than by keyword alone.

source_name: Законодавство України (zakon.rada.gov.ua) — official legal database
why_relevant: The official consolidated text database. Each act has a stable /laws/show/{id} URL, dated consolidated redactions ('редакція від ...'), a 'Прикінцеві та перехідні положення' block carrying entry-into-force and transition deadlines, and a card of amending acts. This is where an adopted bill becomes a citable, versioned law.

source_name: Закон України «Про банки і банківську діяльність» № 2121-III (act page)
why_relevant: The anchor banking statute. Its amendment history page enumerates every adopted law that touched banking regulation, giving a retrospective index of the whole A3 pipeline and the outer deadlines the NBU implements by regulation.

source_name: Закон України «Про платіжні послуги» № 1591-IX (act page)
source_subtype: primary statute with staggered entry-into-force clauses
why_relevant: The PSD2/EMD-aligned payments framework statute — the single most important act for the payments half of this run. Its transitional provisions stagger entry into force of specific blocks (e.g. open banking) across years, which is precisely the deadline structure A3 must track.

source_name: Портал відкритих даних Верховної Ради — набір «Інформація про законопроекти, що зареєстровано у ВРУ» (zpr)
why_relevant: Machine-readable bulk dump of the bill register (observed 115 files, last updated 26.08.2026). Removes all HTML scraping fragility from pipeline monitoring and enables full-history joins on bill number, initiator, committee and stage.

source_name: Портал відкритих даних ВРУ — набір «Нормативно-правова база України» (zak) / база «Законодавство України»
why_relevant: Bulk export of the official legal database itself (observed 61 files, updated 26.08.2026) — lets the legal corpus be held locally and diffed for new redactions instead of hammering zakon.rada.gov.ua.

source_name: Портал відкритих даних ВРУ — API та каталог наборів (ogd)
why_relevant: Documents the machine access contract (dataset passports updated hourly under /ogd/, list.csv/json/xml catalogues, ~610 datasets) and is the discovery surface for further Rada datasets — votes, agendas, sessions, MPs — that enrich bill-stage tracking.

source_name: Rada open data — «Розгляд питань порядку денного» (zal) та «Засідання» (meetings)
why_relevant: Plenary agenda-item and sitting datasets (observed 140 and 115 files) let the pipeline be tied to actual reading dates and vote events, converting 'in committee' into a dated schedule of first/second readings for banking and payments bills.

source_name: Комітет ВРУ з питань фінансів, податкової та митної політики (komfinbank.rada.gov.ua)
why_relevant: The lead committee for banking and payments bills. Site carries meeting agendas, protocols and stenograms, committee decisions/висновки, lists of bills where it is головний or співвиконавець, public-discussion pages for draft laws, and subcommittee structure covering banking, monetary stability and payment systems. Committee conclusions are where a bill's substance is actually reshaped before second reading.

source_name: Офіційний портал Верховної Ради України — новини та повідомлення (rada.gov.ua)
why_relevant: Parliament's own news/повідомлення channel announces adoptions ('Прийнято Закон «Про платіжні послуги»'), first readings and committee recommendations, often with the bill number in the text — a fast, dated, quotable confirmation layer over the register.

source_name: Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine — English-language news section
why_relevant: Selective English rendering of committee recommendations and adoptions ('Committee ... recommends Parliament adopt as a basis draft law on financial restructuring'). Useful for canonical English names of committees, acts and procedural stages, and for briefing non-Ukrainian readers. Coverage is partial, so it supplements rather than replaces the uk feed.

source_name: Кабінет Міністрів України — розділ «Проєкти законів» (kmu.gov.ua/bills)
why_relevant: Government-initiated banking bills appear here (with explanatory materials) at the pre-registration/approval stage, i.e. before or as they enter the Rada register. Since a large share of banking/payments legislation is Cabinet- or NBU-originated, this is the upstream feeder to the parliamentary pipeline.
